A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the change from Plan2Evolve to Self-CriTeach. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and shared methods, datasets, result rows, and robot demonstrations can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original planning evaluations, alignment and teacher–student experiments, token-efficiency measurements, and a UR5e robot demonstration in Sections 7–9 and Appendix A.4–A.6.

after.justification: v2 reports original planning evaluations, training-component and backbone ablations, and quantitative real-robot comparisons, including Tables 1–9 and Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: v1 ends training with supervised fine-tuning. v2 adds subsequent Constrained Policy Optimization using generated domains to define goal-satisfaction rewards and precondition/state-consistency costs (Section 5.4; Algorithm 1). The domain-generation, repair, pruning, and four-part symbolic-to-CoT procedure are retained; the added RL stage is the substantive method change.

E1.justification: The symbolic benchmark tasks, object coverage, and original π0 room demonstration are retained. v2 adds physical wet-lab preparation with water-bath heating and evaluates room and lab tasks under VLM-derived and rule-based logical states (Section 9). These introduce substantive physical-task and imperfect-perception scenarios beyond v1's evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated Mistral-24B, Ministral-8B, and Llama-3.1-8B baselines, plus Self-Distill, Prompt-CoT, Majority Vote, and a PDDL solver in robot comparisons. The 8B distillation comparison disappears. The renamed 30B-Distill retains v1's Distill-4B(30B) results and is not a newly introduced comparator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces three additional RL training epochs, Llama backbone experiments, and controlled robot comparisons with two perception pipelines and predefined execution routines. Existing SFT splits and its five-epoch schedule remain. Separately, A.2.4 changes the reported success criterion from final-state equality with the goal (v1 Equation 9) to final-state inclusion in the goal (v2 Equation 11); implementation changes or recomputation of retained scores are not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons isolating SFT, CPO, DPO, and combined training, a Llama backbone ablation, and robot perception-robustness comparisons. It removes v1's teacher–student and teacher-dependent alignment-quality studies. The raw-symbol control remains as SCTSymbol-4B, and the original 4B SFT model becomes the SFT-only control.

E5.justification: v2 specifies ten trials per real-robot task in Section 9; v1's robot demonstration supplies no trial count. This is newly reported trial information, not evidence of increased repetitions of the earlier experiment. Neither version supplies confidence intervals, significance tests, or training-seed variability.

E6.justification: v1's P2E-4B results, 0.43 overall success and 0.67 progress, remain unchanged as SCTSFT-4B. v2 newly reports full SCT-4B at 0.46 and 0.76, alongside RL, Llama, additional-baseline, and quantitative robot results. P2E-8B, teacher–student, and Distill-8B rows disappear. These additions and removals substantially change the evidence; the added RL stage and revised success definition prevent treating the headline difference as an established same-setting cross-version gain.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal constrained-RL problem with KL and cost constraints, together with domain-specific reward and violation-cost definitions (Section 5.4, Equations 8–10). A.2.4 also substantively changes the mathematical success predicate from equality to subset inclusion. The earlier symbolic-planning, CoT, and SFT formalism largely remains; no new theorems or proofs are supplied.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on SFT-based self-evolution and symbolic-language alignment. v2 makes the dual use of generated domains for supervision and automatic RL rewards central, and adds resistance to imperfect logical states as a headline claim. The conclusion drops v1's teacher–student effectiveness claim and emphasizes self-critiquing through RL.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of SFT–CPO complementarity, CPO's advantage over DPO, noisy-predicate tolerance, and newer models' symbolic capabilities (Sections 8–9 and A.4). Its limitations retain the requirement for a capable base model but replace v1's unresolved alignment-quality limitation with the requirement that tasks admit accurate symbolic representations, particularly excluding difficult continuous constraints.

D1.justification: v2 documents RL hyperparameters, optimizers, and trajectory-sampling settings; newly identifies Adam for the retained SFT schedule; and supplies output-parsing code and an example generated PDDL domain. A.7 adds perception prompts, ground-truth assumptions, and RTDE execution details. The existing π0 fine-tuning description is retained in A.8.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens the research positioning from symbolic supervision to automated reward construction and RL post-training. It adds discussion and references for CPO, PPO, DeepSeekMath, preference learning, and long-horizon RL, plus new perception/model references. The logical-reasoning evaluations by Patel et al. and Hanmeng Liu et al. are removed; most planning-domain literature remains.

P1.justification: The title and method terminology change throughout, and the abstract, introduction, contributions, related work, methodological explanations, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The separate data-construction subsection is merged into symbolic-to-CoT transformation, the ablation narrative is reorganized, and the appendix gains a substantially revised organization around additional implementation and analysis sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with explicit SFT/RL loops, Figure 2 is enlarged and redesigned, and v1's alignment-quality bar chart is removed. v2 adds a two-task robot montage and comparison/ablation tables, introduces colored score-difference superscripts, and separately redisplays Llama results in A.9. The dataset-distribution plots and appendix π0 montage are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds stronger component and backbone controls, quantitative robot comparisons beyond v1's unquantified demonstration, and fuller implementation details, while removing teacher–student evidence. However, Equation 11 changes success to final-state inclusion in the goal while invalid plans still map to the empty set, so the written criterion would accept invalid plans. The PDFs do not establish whether this is merely a formula error or affects reported evaluations. This unresolved issue concerns the primary outcome and prevents a reliable net-quality judgment despite the clear evidential and documentation gains.
